summary: Findings L1/R05, L1/R06 and L1/R12 of /home/claude/cpt-studio-ux-20261103/refute-r2/results.json, each REPRODUCED by its verifier (verdicts verify:L1:R05, verify:L1:R06, verify:L1:R12) and pre-existing on the installed 41e03656d. Each misreads a form the code already declares it reads: R05, the indication heading line inside a titled report is held only when it ends in a full stop, question or exclamation mark (services._statement_line_end), so the same line without its period is today's report; R06, rule 2's attributive compound needs an ASCII '-' (services.COMPOUND_PARTICIPLE_AFTER, _compound_participle), so the hyphen's Unicode spellings read the act word as today's act; R12, cues.NOT_IN_PERSON reads 'not seen in person' but not its hyphenated or contracted forms, and detect's in-person reading lets the phrase clear itself when a lookbehind's one ASCII space or ASCII apostrophe is not there. Each rule below reads the variant exactly as the declared form is read and holds where it holds; wording outside every declared list stays as installed and is recorded as a residual (residuals_measured).

rules.V05: services._time_parts (R8 D8): an indication section of routing's layout (sections.layout's 'indication' kind: 'Indication:', 'Indications:', 'Reason for procedure:', 'Chief complaint:', ...) whose heading line carries text after its heading reads that heading line as the indication's own line ('indication_line', services._time_kind) whatever the line ends with - a full stop, a semicolon, a dash, a word or nothing: inside a titled report too, the line's acts are the indication's (INDICATION_READING, held), never today's. Only the heading line: after it the section reads exactly as before - today's report inside a titled report (D8's trap: today's biopsy under an unterminated 'Indication: surveillance' stays READY) and the indication outside one (the whole paragraph, as before, so a multi-line indication never gives its next line to today's report). The line read is the reflowed one (services.reflow), as before. services._statement_line_end keeps its full-stop test for every other reader (a keyword reads the heading line without it for the indication only), so _time_end - a history or plan section's end - is unchanged: a history section's heading line is already never today's (history from its heading to its end without a final full stop, the line alone with one), and a plan section inside a titled report stays that report's, as PLAN_HEADING has it.
rules.V06: services.COMPOUND_PARTICIPLE_AFTER and services._compound_participle (P1 rule 2; the lead's L3; R2a): the hyphen of an attributive act compound is read in its Unicode spellings too - U+2010 hyphen, U+2011 non-breaking hyphen, U+2012 figure dash, U+2013 en dash, U+2014 em dash (one new name, cues.HYPHEN) - exactly where the ASCII hyphen is read: _attributive_compound (services._acts_in, so the inventory's pass 3 and the engine's own-passage release, engine._states_unread_act), _attributive_position (R2a's doubtful compounds: a field label 'Snare–resected: No', a negated predicate, read only as denials) and _compound_participle (_predicate_participle: the compound's participle is no act predicate). A compound written with a space ('biopsy proven'), a spaced dash or any other character reads as installed. ACTS, BARE_PARTICIPLE and COMPOUND_PREDICATE_BEFORE are unchanged (mention_count reads ACTS: H2 (d) cannot move). The one release is the declared form's own reading: 'The snare–resected sigmoid polyp was not retrieved.' beside today's snare no longer reads a denied snare (a false conflict, Mara's class), as the ASCII control R8 R2 F05 reads it.
rules.V12: cues.NOT_IN_PERSON (R8 D12; read only to hold an E/M reading, detect._not_in_person): 'not seen in (the) office|clinic|person' is also read hyphenated ('not seen in-person', 'in-office', 'in-clinic', the hyphen in V06's spellings) and with its negation contracted ("wasn't seen in person", "isn't seen in person": n't after a letter, with an ASCII or a U+2019 apostrophe); '(patient|pt|she|he) (was|is) not seen' also as "(patient|pt|she|he) (wasn't|isn't) seen"; and 'no in-person' takes V06's hyphen spellings. detect._PV1_ATTENDANCE reads the contraction ("n't seen") and those hyphens as it reads 'not seen' and 'no in-person', so a variant takes its plain form's path (another time or another service in its clause still clears it, as for the plain form). detect._pv1_todays_mode no longer lets an in-person reading (_PV1_IN_PERSON) that overlaps the NOT_IN_PERSON match being judged clear that match: the phrase's own words are no statement of an in-person visit ('Patient not  seen in person today.' with two spaces, a line break inside the phrase, or "wasn’t seen in person": the fixed-width lookbehinds (?<!not ) and (?<!n't ) read one ASCII space and an ASCII apostrophe only). Hold-only: nothing that clears a C4 hold reads more ('seen in-person today' with a Unicode hyphen clears nothing, as installed).
